deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Gauss manuscript. It is the first page of the printed table of contents ('Inhalt') of an 18th-century German arithmetic and algebra textbook. It is almost certainly Christian Leiste's 'Die Arithmetic und Algebra' (Wolfenbüttel, 1790), which the bundle name 'HB.Leiste' points to. The previous page is the end of the book's historical preface: Bernoulli, l'Hôpital, Manfredi, Leibniz's Interusurium, and Euler's death in 1783, with a reference to the ALZ of 1785.

The page lists the following sections:
- Introduction: §1 the concept and division of pure and applied mathematics; §2 mathematical method.
- First Section, Part I: how to express magnitude as number (§3–6). This covers numbers, numerals and numeration, a preliminary account of ratios, and magnitude as a relative concept.
- First Section, Part II, item 1: addition and subtraction (§7–8).
- First Section, Part II, item 2: multiplication (§9–13); division (§14–16); principles (§17–19); the definition of a fraction (§20).

The one mathematical item is §21–24, 'the general expression of number (am+n)/m'. Here a, m and n are integers with m > 0 (my reading). The expression is meant to cover:
- whole numbers (n = 0, or n a multiple of m), giving a;
- proper fractions (a = 0, 0 < n < m);
- improper fractions (a ≥ 1, 0 < n < m), i.e. the mixed number a + n/m.

The implied identity is (am+n)/m = a + n/m, which is just Euclidean division of the numerator by m.

There is no derivation, calculation or annotation in Gauss's hand on this page. The text in the left margin is bleed-through from the facing printed page.

results.what: Representation of any rational number as (am+n)/m = a + n/m, used to treat whole numbers, proper fractions and improper fractions uniformly (textbook §21–24).
Table of contents of an elementary arithmetic textbook: numeration, ratios, the four operations, fractions.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed table of contents from a contemporary textbook (probably Leiste's Arithmetic and Algebra), not Gauss's own work. It contains no handwritten notes and only routine elementary material.

checkable.asserts: The general expression (am+n)/m equals the mixed number a + n/m (should simplify to 0).
An example with a=3, m=7, n=2: the improper fraction 23/7 equals 3 2/7.

transcription_corrections: In §II.1 the print reads 'turch Zahlen' (a typesetting slip for 'durch'); the transcription silently normalized it to 'durch'.
'§. 25.' at the bottom is the catchword for the next page (where it reads '§. 25–27'), not a separate entry.
The marginal text on the left ('...s erlangt haben, ...yden Erfindern' etc.) is the facing preface page XVI, not part of this page.
